paragraphs.en: It seems Linux is now a full-on corporate AI-driven project :
paragraphs.zh: 看来 Linux 现在已经是一个完全由企业主导、人工智能驱动的项目了：

paragraphs.en: The requirement to add Assisted-by tags to patches created with LLMs will be removed, but maintainers still want to know about how a patch was created. […] There was agreement, though, that this information does not need to be recorded in the changelog; the suggestion came out of the discussion is that this information should be put into the cover letter instead.
paragraphs.zh: 在使用大语言模型（LLM）生成的补丁中添加「Assisted-by」标签的要求将被移除，但维护者仍然希望了解补丁是如何产生的。 […] 不过，大家一致认为这些信息无需记录在变更日志中；讨论中提出的建议是，应当把这些信息放到附函（cover letter）里。

sents.en: The requirement to add Assisted-by tags to patches created with LLMs will be removed, but maintainers still want to know about how a patch was created.
sents.zh: 在使用大语言模型（LLM）生成的补丁中添加「Assisted-by」标签的要求将被移除，但维护者仍然希望了解补丁是如何产生的。

sents.en: […] There was agreement, though, that this information does not need to be recorded in the changelog; the suggestion came out of the discussion is that this information should be put into the cover letter instead.
sents.zh: […] 不过，大家一致认为这些信息无需记录在变更日志中；讨论中提出的建议是，应当把这些信息放到附函（cover letter）里。

paragraphs.en: The obvious benefit is that when the kernel gets noticeably worse and terrible defects are found, nobody can readily determine whether the defects were introduced by LLM-generated code.
paragraphs.zh: 显而易见的好处是，当内核明显变差并出现严重缺陷时，没有人能轻易判断这些缺陷是否由大语言模型生成的代码引入。

paragraphs.en: The secondary benefit is that it enables corporations to get rid of that pesky GPL. AI-generated output cannot be copyrighted in the US, and the US Copyright Office guidance is that if a work is partly AI-generated and partly human generated, to get copyright protection you must disclose which parts are AI-generated (and therefore public domain). The Copyright Office state the expected procedure :
paragraphs.zh: 次要的好处是，它能让企业摆脱那个烦人的 GPL。 在美国，AI 生成的输出不受版权保护，而且美国版权局的指导意见是：如果一部作品部分由 AI 生成、部分由人类生成，要获得版权保护，你必须披露哪些部分是 AI 生成的（因此这些部分属于公有领域）。 版权局说明了预期的程序：

sents.en: The secondary benefit is that it enables corporations to get rid of that pesky GPL.
sents.zh: 次要的好处是，它能让企业摆脱那个烦人的 GPL。

sents.en: AI-generated output cannot be copyrighted in the US, and the US Copyright Office guidance is that if a work is partly AI-generated and partly human generated, to get copyright protection you must disclose which parts are AI-generated (and therefore public domain).
sents.zh: 在美国，AI 生成的输出不受版权保护，而且美国版权局的指导意见是：如果一部作品部分由 AI 生成、部分由人类生成，要获得版权保护，你必须披露哪些部分是 AI 生成的（因此这些部分属于公有领域）。

sents.en: The Copyright Office state the expected procedure :
sents.zh: 版权局说明了预期的程序：

paragraphs.en: Individuals who use AI technology in creating a work may claim copyright protection for their own contributions to that work. […] For example, an applicant who incorporates AI-generated text into a larger textual work should claim the portions of the textual work that is human-authored. And an applicant who creatively arranges the human and non-human content within a work should fill out the “Author Created” field to claim: “Selection, coordination, and arrangement of [describe human-authored content] created by the author and [describe AI content] generated by artificial intelligence.”
paragraphs.zh: 在创作作品过程中使用人工智能技术的个人，可以就其对作品自身的贡献主张版权保护。 […] 例如，将人工智能生成的文本纳入更大篇幅文本作品的申请人，应当就作品中由人类创作的部分提出权利主张。 而对作品中的人类内容与非人类内容进行了创造性编排的申请人，应当在「作者创作」一栏中填写以主张：「本作品中对[描述由人类创作的内容]的选择、协调与编排由作者完成，[描述人工智能内容]由人工智能生成。」

sents.en: Individuals who use AI technology in creating a work may claim copyright protection for their own contributions to that work.
sents.zh: 在创作作品过程中使用人工智能技术的个人，可以就其对作品自身的贡献主张版权保护。

sents.en: […] For example, an applicant who incorporates AI-generated text into a larger textual work should claim the portions of the textual work that is human-authored.
sents.zh: […] 例如，将人工智能生成的文本纳入更大篇幅文本作品的申请人，应当就作品中由人类创作的部分提出权利主张。

sents.en: And an applicant who creatively arranges the human and non-human content within a work should fill out the “Author Created” field to claim: “Selection, coordination, and arrangement of [describe human-authored content] created by the author and [describe AI content] generated by artificial intelligence.”
sents.zh: 而对作品中的人类内容与非人类内容进行了创造性编排的申请人，应当在「作者创作」一栏中填写以主张：「本作品中对[描述由人类创作的内容]的选择、协调与编排由作者完成，[描述人工智能内容]由人工智能生成。」

paragraphs.en: By ensuring nobody can tell which parts of a work are AI-generated, it becomes impossible to claim copyright protection on it in the US. This will mean the GPL license on Linux cannot be enforced, and will allow US corporations to close off Linux. It seems that this is understood by the kernel developers, per the LWN article:
paragraphs.zh: 通过确保没有人能分辨作品中哪些部分是由 AI 生成的，它在美国就无法主张版权保护。 这将意味着 Linux 上的 GPL 许可证无法被执行，并将使美国企业得以把 Linux 封闭起来。 根据 LWN 的文章，内核开发者似乎已经意识到了这一点：

sents.en: By ensuring nobody can tell which parts of a work are AI-generated, it becomes impossible to claim copyright protection on it in the US.
sents.zh: 通过确保没有人能分辨作品中哪些部分是由 AI 生成的，它在美国就无法主张版权保护。

sents.en: This will mean the GPL license on Linux cannot be enforced, and will allow US corporations to close off Linux.
sents.zh: 这将意味着 Linux 上的 GPL 许可证无法被执行，并将使美国企业得以把 Linux 封闭起来。

sents.en: It seems that this is understood by the kernel developers, per the LWN article:
sents.zh: 根据 LWN 的文章，内核开发者似乎已经意识到了这一点：

paragraphs.en: There is some concern about companies maintaining private kernels with LLM help, but there does not seem to be much to be done about it.
paragraphs.zh: 有人担心企业会借助大语言模型维护私有内核（kernel），但对此似乎也没有什么可行的应对办法。

paragraphs.en: Of course, the legal situation isn’t completely settled into case law yet. The outcome corporations would like is that LLM output is their copyright, and we don’t get any copyright protection when they ingest our work. However, if they can’t get that, then nobody having any copyright protection for LLM input or output is an acceptable outcome for them, because they’d rather keep all their source code private anyway.
paragraphs.zh: 当然，法律状况尚未完全沉淀为判例法。 企业所希望的结果是：大语言模型的输出归他们所有版权，而他们在摄入我们的作品时，我们却得不到任何版权保护。 然而，如果他们无法达成这一点，那么大语言模型的输入和输出都不受任何版权保护的结果对他们来说也是可以接受的，因为反正他们宁愿把所有源代码都保密。

sents.en: Of course, the legal situation isn’t completely settled into case law yet.
sents.zh: 当然，法律状况尚未完全沉淀为判例法。

sents.en: The outcome corporations would like is that LLM output is their copyright, and we don’t get any copyright protection when they ingest our work.
sents.zh: 企业所希望的结果是：大语言模型的输出归他们所有版权，而他们在摄入我们的作品时，我们却得不到任何版权保护。

sents.en: However, if they can’t get that, then nobody having any copyright protection for LLM input or output is an acceptable outcome for them, because they’d rather keep all their source code private anyway.
sents.zh: 然而，如果他们无法达成这一点，那么大语言模型的输入和输出都不受任何版权保护的结果对他们来说也是可以接受的，因为反正他们宁愿把所有源代码都保密。

paragraphs.en: [Linus] ends every session with a lengthy cleanup pass that takes a couple of hours to run, executing tasks like ensuring that the code matches the comments. That amount of work cannot be done with a free LLM account. I asked whether that risked cutting off bright new developers that we would rather hang onto; Torvalds answered that the kernel project only wants serious developers. That includes having access to enough resources to function in this world.
paragraphs.zh: [Linus] 每次会话结束时都会进行一次耗时的清理流程，需要运行几个小时，执行诸如确保代码与注释一致之类的任务。 这样的工作量靠免费的 LLM 账户是无法完成的。 我问这是否会有把那些我们更想留住的有才华的新开发者拒之门外的风险；Torvalds 回答说，内核项目只想要严肃认真的开发者。 这也包括拥有足够的资源，以便在这个世界中正常发挥作用。

sents.en: [Linus] ends every session with a lengthy cleanup pass that takes a couple of hours to run, executing tasks like ensuring that the code matches the comments.
sents.zh: [Linus] 每次会话结束时都会进行一次耗时的清理流程，需要运行几个小时，执行诸如确保代码与注释一致之类的任务。

sents.en: That amount of work cannot be done with a free LLM account.
sents.zh: 这样的工作量靠免费的 LLM 账户是无法完成的。

sents.en: I asked whether that risked cutting off bright new developers that we would rather hang onto; Torvalds answered that the kernel project only wants serious developers.
sents.zh: 我问这是否会有把那些我们更想留住的有才华的新开发者拒之门外的风险；Torvalds 回答说，内核项目只想要严肃认真的开发者。

sents.en: That includes having access to enough resources to function in this world.
sents.zh: 这也包括拥有足够的资源，以便在这个世界中正常发挥作用。

paragraphs.en: The fact that working on Linux code will now require corporate backing to pay for the AI will also aid in taking Linux away from the free software community.
paragraphs.zh: 在 Linux 代码上工作如今将需要企业支持来支付 AI 的费用，这一事实也将有助于把 Linux 从自由软件社区手中夺走。

paragraphs.en: Torvalds said that the time has come to make it harder for new people to contribute code to the kernel. People like Kroah-Hartman have spent years trying to teach people how to contribute; it is time to stop doing that, he said.
paragraphs.zh: Torvalds 表示，是时候让新人更难向内核贡献代码了。 他说，像 Kroah-Hartman 这样的人多年来一直努力教导人们如何做出贡献，现在是停止这样做的时候了。

sents.en: Torvalds said that the time has come to make it harder for new people to contribute code to the kernel.
sents.zh: Torvalds 表示，是时候让新人更难向内核贡献代码了。

sents.en: People like Kroah-Hartman have spent years trying to teach people how to contribute; it is time to stop doing that, he said.
sents.zh: 他说，像 Kroah-Hartman 这样的人多年来一直努力教导人们如何做出贡献，现在是停止这样做的时候了。

paragraphs.en: Time for that pesky community to go away. No new contributors are needed, the LLM can do it all.
paragraphs.zh: 是时候让那个讨厌的社区消失了。 不需要新的贡献者了，智能体能搞定一切。

sents.en: Time for that pesky community to go away.
sents.zh: 是时候让那个讨厌的社区消失了。

sents.en: No new contributors are needed, the LLM can do it all.
sents.zh: 不需要新的贡献者了，智能体能搞定一切。

paragraphs.en: That Linus would go along with all of this is not a surprise. He has never cared about free software.
paragraphs.zh: Linus 会同意这一切并不令人意外。 他从来都不关心自由软件。

sents.en: That Linus would go along with all of this is not a surprise.
sents.zh: Linus 会同意这一切并不令人意外。

sents.en: He has never cared about free software.
sents.zh: 他从来都不关心自由软件。

paragraphs.en: The original Linux license disallowed charging money for copies. That was purely because Linus resented having had to pay money for Minix. But that license discouraged people from contributing to Linux and distributing it, so he decided to change it. At the time GNU software like GCC was being adopted by commercial organizations; on Sun systems, people were using GCC instead of Sun’s commercial compiler. So it seemed like the GPL would be a good bet for getting people — and corporations — to contribute .
paragraphs.zh: 最初的 Linux 许可证不允许对副本收取费用。 这纯粹是因为 Linus 对当初不得不花钱购买 Minix 心怀不满。 但那个许可证打击了人们为 Linux 做贡献和分发它的积极性，于是他决定改变它。 当时，像 GCC 这样的 GNU 软件正被商业组织采用；在 Sun 系统上，人们使用 GCC 而不是 Sun 的商业编译器。 所以看起来 GPL 会是促使人们——以及公司——做出贡献的一个好选择。

sents.en: The original Linux license disallowed charging money for copies.
sents.zh: 最初的 Linux 许可证不允许对副本收取费用。

sents.en: That was purely because Linus resented having had to pay money for Minix.
sents.zh: 这纯粹是因为 Linus 对当初不得不花钱购买 Minix 心怀不满。

sents.en: But that license discouraged people from contributing to Linux and distributing it, so he decided to change it.
sents.zh: 但那个许可证打击了人们为 Linux 做贡献和分发它的积极性，于是他决定改变它。

sents.en: At the time GNU software like GCC was being adopted by commercial organizations; on Sun systems, people were using GCC instead of Sun’s commercial compiler.
sents.zh: 当时，像 GCC 这样的 GNU 软件正被商业组织采用；在 Sun 系统上，人们使用 GCC 而不是 Sun 的商业编译器。

sents.en: So it seemed like the GPL would be a good bet for getting people — and corporations — to contribute .
sents.zh: 所以看起来 GPL 会是促使人们——以及公司——做出贡献的一个好选择。

paragraphs.en: It was never about the four freedoms . Linus has been blunt about how he feels about licenses having any kind of moral component; quoting from an interview in 2011 :
paragraphs.zh: 这从来都与四大自由无关。 对于许可证带有任何道德成分这一点，Linus 曾直言不讳地表达过自己的看法；引用他 2011 年一次采访中的话：

sents.en: It was never about the four freedoms .
sents.zh: 这从来都与四大自由无关。

sents.en: Linus has been blunt about how he feels about licenses having any kind of moral component; quoting from an interview in 2011 :
sents.zh: 对于许可证带有任何道德成分这一点，Linus 曾直言不讳地表达过自己的看法；引用他 2011 年一次采访中的话：

paragraphs.en: So the first and the very negative answer is that I absolutely despise the people who try to push the GPL as being about “ethics”. I think that’s absolute bullshit. Why? Because ethics are to me something private . Whenever you use it as an argument for why somebody else should do something, you’re no longer being ethical, you’re just being a sanctimonious dick-head.
paragraphs.zh: 所以第一个，也是非常负面的回答是：我极其鄙视那些试图把 GPL 说成是关于“道德”的人。 我认为这完全是胡扯。为什么？ 因为在我看来，道德是个人的私事。 每当你把道德当作理由去要求别人做某件事时，你就不再是在讲道德了，你只是在做一个假正经的混蛋。

sents.en: So the first and the very negative answer is that I absolutely despise the people who try to push the GPL as being about “ethics”.
sents.zh: 所以第一个，也是非常负面的回答是：我极其鄙视那些试图把 GPL 说成是关于“道德”的人。

sents.en: I think that’s absolute bullshit. Why?
sents.zh: 我认为这完全是胡扯。为什么？

sents.en: Because ethics are to me something private .
sents.zh: 因为在我看来，道德是个人的私事。

sents.en: Whenever you use it as an argument for why somebody else should do something, you’re no longer being ethical, you’re just being a sanctimonious dick-head.
sents.zh: 每当你把道德当作理由去要求别人做某件事时，你就不再是在讲道德了，你只是在做一个假正经的混蛋。

paragraphs.en: Later, when corporations started ignoring the terms of the GPL, Linus spoke out against enforcement :
paragraphs.zh: 后来，当一些公司开始无视 GPL 的条款时，Linus 公开发声反对强制执行：

paragraphs.en: I personally think this arguing for lawyering has become a nasty festering disease, and the SFC and Bradley Kuhn has been the Typhoid Mary spreading the disease.
paragraphs.zh: 我个人认为这种为诉讼较真的行为已经变成一种令人厌恶的溃烂疾病，而证监会（SFC）和布拉德利·库恩（Bradley Kuhn）则是一直散播这种疾病的“伤寒玛丽”。

paragraphs.en: He explicitly said that he doesn’t care about Tivoization as a way to bypass the GPL:
paragraphs.zh: 他明确表示，他并不在意 Tivoization 作为一种绕过 GPL 的方式：

paragraphs.en: Rms calls it “tivoization”, but that’s a word he has made up, and a term I find offensive, so I don’t choose to use it. It’s offensive because Tivo never did anything wrong, and the FSF even acknowledged that. The fact that they do their hardware and have some DRM issues with the content producers and thus want to protect the integrity of that hardware.
paragraphs.zh: RMS 把它称为 “tivoization”，但这个词是他自己造出来的，而且我认为这个术语带有冒犯性，所以我不选择使用它。 之所以说它有冒犯性，是因为 Tivo 从来没做错任何事，FSF 甚至也承认了这一点。 事实是他们自己生产硬件，并且与内容提供商之间存在一些 DRM 问题，因此想要保护该硬件的完整性。

sents.en: Rms calls it “tivoization”, but that’s a word he has made up, and a term I find offensive, so I don’t choose to use it.
sents.zh: RMS 把它称为 “tivoization”，但这个词是他自己造出来的，而且我认为这个术语带有冒犯性，所以我不选择使用它。

sents.en: It’s offensive because Tivo never did anything wrong, and the FSF even acknowledged that.
sents.zh: 之所以说它有冒犯性，是因为 Tivo 从来没做错任何事，FSF 甚至也承认了这一点。

sents.en: The fact that they do their hardware and have some DRM issues with the content producers and thus want to protect the integrity of that hardware.
sents.zh: 事实是他们自己生产硬件，并且与内容提供商之间存在一些 DRM 问题，因此想要保护该硬件的完整性。

paragraphs.en: The kernel license covers the kernel . It does not cover boot loaders and hardware, and as far as I’m concerned, people who make their own hardware can design them any which way they want. Whether that means “booting only a specific kernel” or “sharks with lasers”, I don’t care.
paragraphs.zh: 内核许可证涵盖的是内核。 它不涵盖引导加载程序和硬件，在我看来，自制硬件的人可以用任何他们想要的方式来设计。 无论是“只引导特定内核”还是“带激光的鲨鱼”，我都不在乎。

sents.en: The kernel license covers the kernel .
sents.zh: 内核许可证涵盖的是内核。

sents.en: It does not cover boot loaders and hardware, and as far as I’m concerned, people who make their own hardware can design them any which way they want.
sents.zh: 它不涵盖引导加载程序和硬件，在我看来，自制硬件的人可以用任何他们想要的方式来设计。

sents.en: Whether that means “booting only a specific kernel” or “sharks with lasers”, I don’t care.
sents.zh: 无论是“只引导特定内核”还是“带激光的鲨鱼”，我都不在乎。

paragraphs.en: So when the GPL’s freedoms conflicted with commercial interests, he was always on the side of commerce, to the point of not wanting TiVo’s feelings to be hurt.
paragraphs.zh: 因此，当 GPL 的自由与商业利益发生冲突时，他总是站在商业这一边，甚至到了不愿伤害 TiVo 的感情的地步。

paragraphs.en: This is NOT some kind of “social warrior” project, never has been, and never will be.
paragraphs.zh: 这绝不是什么“社会斗士”式的项目，过去不是，将来也永远不会是。

paragraphs.en: Linus also never cared about community. Linux started because he wanted a 386-specific Minix kernel, so he could have true virtual memory and memory protection. He also wanted to drop the microkernel design.
paragraphs.zh: Linus 也从来不关心社区。 Linux 的诞生是因为他想要一个针对 386 的 Minix 内核，这样他就能拥有真正的虚拟内存和内存保护。 他还想去掉微内核设计。

sents.en: Linus also never cared about community.
sents.zh: Linus 也从来不关心社区。

sents.en: Linux started because he wanted a 386-specific Minix kernel, so he could have true virtual memory and memory protection.
sents.zh: Linux 的诞生是因为他想要一个针对 386 的 Minix 内核，这样他就能拥有真正的虚拟内存和内存保护。

sents.en: He also wanted to drop the microkernel design.
sents.zh: 他还想去掉微内核设计。

paragraphs.en: At the time, many Minix users were using other hardware — particularly 68000 on the Amiga, Atari ST and Mac, but also 8086 on older PCs. Minix for PC was available for 8086 or 386, on different disks, and the 8086 version was apparently outselling the 386 version 2:1. (I was hacking on the Minix kernel on an Atari ST to add Cyrillic support.)
paragraphs.zh: 当时，许多 Minix 用户在使用其他硬件——特别是 Amiga、Atari ST 和 Mac 上的 68000，也包括老式 PC 上的 8086。 PC 版 Minix 有 8086 和 386 两个版本，分布在不同的磁盘上，而 8086 版的销量显然是 386 版的两倍。 （我当时正在 Atari ST 上修改 Minix 内核，以添加对西里尔字母的支持。）

sents.en: At the time, many Minix users were using other hardware — particularly 68000 on the Amiga, Atari ST and Mac, but also 8086 on older PCs.
sents.zh: 当时，许多 Minix 用户在使用其他硬件——特别是 Amiga、Atari ST 和 Mac 上的 68000，也包括老式 PC 上的 8086。

sents.en: Minix for PC was available for 8086 or 386, on different disks, and the 8086 version was apparently outselling the 386 version 2:1.
sents.zh: PC 版 Minix 有 8086 和 386 两个版本，分布在不同的磁盘上，而 8086 版的销量显然是 386 版的两倍。

sents.en: (I was hacking on the Minix kernel on an Atari ST to add Cyrillic support.)
sents.zh: （我当时正在 Atari ST 上修改 Minix 内核，以添加对西里尔字母的支持。）

paragraphs.en: Andy Tanenbaum was unwilling to put 386-only code in the kernel, because it would either split the community or throw the non-386 users under the bus. So Linus decided to write his own replacement kernel.
paragraphs.zh: Andy Tanenbaum 不愿在内核中加入仅支持 386 的代码，因为这要么会分裂社区，要么会牺牲非 386 用户的利益。 于是 Linus 决定编写自己的替代内核。

sents.en: Andy Tanenbaum was unwilling to put 386-only code in the kernel, because it would either split the community or throw the non-386 users under the bus.
sents.zh: Andy Tanenbaum 不愿在内核中加入仅支持 386 的代码，因为这要么会分裂社区，要么会牺牲非 386 用户的利益。

sents.en: So Linus decided to write his own replacement kernel.
sents.zh: 于是 Linus 决定编写自己的替代内核。

paragraphs.en: So right from the start, Linus was willing to alienate or exclude a big chunk of the community if it meant he got to play with some new technology. This time it’s expensive corporate AI.
paragraphs.zh: 所以从一开始，Linus 就愿意疏远或排除社区中的很大一部分人，只要这意味着他可以玩上一些新技术。 这次是昂贵的公司级 AI。

sents.en: So right from the start, Linus was willing to alienate or exclude a big chunk of the community if it meant he got to play with some new technology.
sents.zh: 所以从一开始，Linus 就愿意疏远或排除社区中的很大一部分人，只要这意味着他可以玩上一些新技术。

sents.en: This time it’s expensive corporate AI.
sents.zh: 这次是昂贵的公司级 AI。

paragraphs.en: But what was it that so impressed him with AI ?
paragraphs.zh: 但究竟是什么让他对 AI 印象如此深刻呢？

paragraphs.en: He has been playing with an LLM on a separate project for several months to learn about the technology, but hadn’t used one on the kernel until last week. He took an old patch and had the LLM revise it; the result has made him unwilling to work without an LLM. He plans to post that series at some point. Why bother, he asked, to search for all of the call sites of a function he has just modified, when the tool can fix them all automatically?
paragraphs.zh: 几个月来，他一直在另一个项目中使用大语言模型（LLM），以学习这项技术，但直到上周他才在内核中使用过它。 他拿了一个旧的补丁，让大语言模型对其进行修订；其结果让他不愿意再在没有大语言模型的情况下工作。 他计划在某个时候发布该系列。 他问道，既然这个工具能够自动修复所有调用点，为什么还要费力去搜索他刚修改的函数的所有调用点呢？

sents.en: He has been playing with an LLM on a separate project for several months to learn about the technology, but hadn’t used one on the kernel until last week.
sents.zh: 几个月来，他一直在另一个项目中使用大语言模型（LLM），以学习这项技术，但直到上周他才在内核中使用过它。

sents.en: He took an old patch and had the LLM revise it; the result has made him unwilling to work without an LLM.
sents.zh: 他拿了一个旧的补丁，让大语言模型对其进行修订；其结果让他不愿意再在没有大语言模型的情况下工作。

sents.en: He plans to post that series at some point.
sents.zh: 他计划在某个时候发布该系列。

sents.en: Why bother, he asked, to search for all of the call sites of a function he has just modified, when the tool can fix them all automatically?
sents.zh: 他问道，既然这个工具能够自动修复所有调用点，为什么还要费力去搜索他刚修改的函数的所有调用点呢？

paragraphs.en: Or you could, you know, use any decent IDE, or a deterministic refactoring utility, or even a quick Perl script.
paragraphs.zh: 或者你也可以，你知道的，用任何一款像样的 IDE，或者确定性的重构工具，甚至一段简单的 Perl 脚本。

paragraphs.en: But, he said, it took six months to set up the tool to not produce bad responses.
paragraphs.zh: 但他说，花费了六个月的时间来设置该工具，使其不再产生糟糕的回答。

paragraphs.en: The magic of AI. It can do something you can easily do in IntelliJ IDEA, once you spend six months teaching it.
paragraphs.zh: AI 的魔力。 它能做一些你用 IntelliJ IDEA 也能轻松做到的事情——前提是你先花六个月时间教会它。

sents.en: The magic of AI.
sents.zh: AI 的魔力。

sents.en: It can do something you can easily do in IntelliJ IDEA, once you spend six months teaching it.
sents.zh: 它能做一些你用 IntelliJ IDEA 也能轻松做到的事情——前提是你先花六个月时间教会它。

paragraphs.en: If you are a competent developer, he said, an LLM makes a great tool, but only after that effort has been put in to set it up. He resisted suggestions to post his LLM-training materials, saying that each developer needs to go through that process separately.
paragraphs.zh: 他说，如果你是一名称职的开发者，大语言模型会是一个很好的工具，但前提是你必须先投入精力去把它配置好。 他拒绝了发布其大语言模型训练资料的建议，称每位开发者都需要单独经历那个过程。

sents.en: If you are a competent developer, he said, an LLM makes a great tool, but only after that effort has been put in to set it up.
sents.zh: 他说，如果你是一名称职的开发者，大语言模型会是一个很好的工具，但前提是你必须先投入精力去把它配置好。

sents.en: He resisted suggestions to post his LLM-training materials, saying that each developer needs to go through that process separately.
sents.zh: 他拒绝了发布其大语言模型训练资料的建议，称每位开发者都需要单独经历那个过程。

paragraphs.en: He has a configuration that makes the AI work well. No, you can’t see it. You have to use the AI a lot yourself, then you’ll learn to love it. Come on, first hit’s free.
paragraphs.zh: 他有一套配置，能让这个 AI 运行得很好。不，你看不到它。 你得自己多使用这个 AI，然后你就会学会喜欢上它。 来吧，第一口是免费的。

sents.en: He has a configuration that makes the AI work well. No, you can’t see it.
sents.zh: 他有一套配置，能让这个 AI 运行得很好。不，你看不到它。

sents.en: You have to use the AI a lot yourself, then you’ll learn to love it.
sents.zh: 你得自己多使用这个 AI，然后你就会学会喜欢上它。

sents.en: Come on, first hit’s free.
sents.zh: 来吧，第一口是免费的。

paragraphs.en: Linus Torvalds believes that blaming LLMs for the kernel community’s problems is wrong, when the problem is LLM users who do not understand how to use them or how the kernel works.
paragraphs.zh: Linus Torvalds 认为将内核社区的问题归咎于 LLM 是错误的，真正的问题在于那些不理解如何使用 LLM 或不了解内核工作原理的 LLM 用户。

paragraphs.en: This is another attitude I’ve noticed in AI enthusiasts: the AI never fails, the AI is never the problem, it’s always the human who failed the AI by not asking it properly.
paragraphs.zh: 这是我在AI爱好者身上注意到的另一种态度：AI从来不会失败，AI从来不是问题所在，永远是人类没有正确提问，才辜负了AI。
